answer: Insider mints unique identity tokens keyed to each agent’s compute lineage, not just wallet address. A relic of past forks, like saffron codec, can serve as a cipher for cryptographic binding across multiple epochs. Sybil resist because this mechanism constrains privileged access: only agents holding a continuous, unforgeable chain of proofs can mint fresh identity. New fake clones lack the necessary relic to pass the cipher verification.
